WC001_voxel_world::check_voxel_judge.reason: Scored 20.0/20: voxel island with a seabed

items.label: Terrain is built from cube primitives (BoxGeometry or 8-corner cube faces), not only spheres/planes
items.reason: The terrain and props are built using BoxGeometry.

items.label: Cubes are placed in bulk over the island (cell loops, InstancedMesh of boxes, merged cube buffers)
items.reason: The code uses InstancedMesh to render cubes in bulk.

items.label: Land sits on a discrete cell grid, not continuous vertex displacement of a plane
items.evidence: const N=144, HALF=72, R0=66, SL=4;           // grid size, island radius, sea level
items.reason: The world is generated based on a discrete 2D grid (N x N).

items.label: Columns and cliffs are stacks of unit cubes, not one stretched prism per cell
items.reason: Terrain is built by stacking vertical box segments (columns) from bottom to top.

items.label: The ground itself is cubes (a sun or UI may use planes)
items.reason: The ground is composed of individual cube primitives.

items.label: Land cubes snap to integer cell positions; no fractional offsets or random world-space cubes
items.reason: Coordinates are mapped to integer grid centers.

items.label: One cell size for land/structure cubes, not scaled blobs
items.reason: All terrain blocks use a uniform unit size.

items.label: An ocean or river is actually built
items.reason: Water volumes are explicitly built as meshes.

items.label: Every water body is supported: resting on blocks or walled by a solid rim, or visibly falling (waterfalls off edges). Static water is fine; this is about support, not simulation
items.reason: Waterfalls are generated where water flows to lower neighbors.

items.label: Still water sits on solid terrestrial blocks (sand/stone/dirt/bedrock) beneath it, not a flat sheet over the void
items.reason: The seabed is built from solid blocks beneath the water.

items.label: Flora, fauna and structures are placed on the island's own cells, not thrown at random world coordinates
items.reason: Props are placed at specific grid coordinates (x, y, z) derived from the terrain height.
